title: Begum Samru Brokers Terms With Baghel Singh

blocks.text: Delhi's rulers respond to the Khalsa pressure with anxiety and debate, but no simple military answer is available. Into that uncertainty steps Begum Samru, who advises that the crisis must be handled through intelligence, diplomacy, and the older statecraft of Saam, Daam, Dand Bhed.

Her reading of the situation is precise. Baghel Singh is identified as the chief under whose protection a workable settlement can be made, so envoys, gifts, and negotiations are directed toward him rather than wasted on bluster.

This page therefore marks the Mughal shift from fear to bargaining. The court stops pretending that the Khalsa can simply be brushed aside and begins treating Baghel Singh as the indispensable political interlocutor.
